lines.intro: Bitcoin is public. Every payment leaves a trail. OpenSwap helps you leave a lighter one.
lines.route: Here's how a swap works. Your coins travel through a circle of routers, and come back as different coins, with no link to where they started. Every message travels over Tor.
lines.legacy: Legacy is the original atomic swap. Both sides lock their coins in a shared contract. Either the swap completes, or everyone gets a refund.
lines.taproot: Taproot swaps look like ordinary payments on chain. The backup scripts stay hidden unless they're needed, and claims take about a quarter less space, so you pay lower fees.
lines.payswap: PaySwap lets you swap and pay in one step. The coins go straight to the person you're paying, and they receive exactly the amount you set.
lines.market: Routers live in an open marketplace. They announce themselves on Nostr, so there's no central server to shut down. Each router locks up a fidelity bond to stay honest, cheaters get banned, and your wallet picks the cheapest routers first.
lines.deploy: Portal runs as a desktop app, or on a small server at home that you can reach from any browser.
lines.backend: It reads the chain through Electrum, or your own Bitcoin node. For extra privacy, you can connect to Electrum over Tor.
lines.wallet: In the wallet, choose an amount and the number of routers. You see the fees before you start. Then the swap runs through the circle, and your coins come home.
lines.router: Running a router is how you earn. Lock a bond, join the market, and every swap you route pays you a fee. It runs quietly in the background... earning while you sleep.
lines.cta: Download Portal at open swap dot live.
lines.thanks: OpenSwap is built in the open, by a small team and many contributors. Thank you.
lines.lightning: And next... Lightning swaps are on the way.
lines.outro: Privacy is necessary for an open society in the electronic age.
